- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; cap forecast at +2% above peak or use moving average of last 5 days.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is trending downward, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10-day moving average of prior 10 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 3–5 days are above true outcome, apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 0.5–1.5% per day from forecasted values starting from day 3.
- When sentiment is negative (though not present in examples), model tends to underpredict; if sentiment is neutral, assume slight upward bias and adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for 30-day horizon.
